# Compute the equi-independence number of the hypercube

<!-- Generated by MathResearchLab. This file is rewritten on every sync; edit the app, not this file. -->

**Status:** Open per source; openness not yet verified

## Statement

Original wording (verbatim from the source):

```latex
{\em Calculate $\alpha_=(\hyp{n})$.}
```

Normalized:

Determine $\alpha_=(Q_n)$ for all $n$: the maximum size of an independent set of $Q_n$ that contains equally many vertices of even and of odd Hamming weight.

Source: Feliú Sagols, Guillermo Morales-Luna, *Parity balance of the $i$-th dimension edges in Hamiltonian cycles of the hypercube*, arXiv:1009.3304, doi:10.48550/arxiv.1009.3304, p. 8, Conclusions

## Definitions

- **equi-independence number $\alpha_=(G)$**: For a bipartite graph $G$: the cardinality of a maximum independent set with half of its vertices in each bipartition class.

## Known results

- $\alpha_=(Q_n)\ge 2^{n-2}$ for $n\ge3$. *(Feliú Sagols, Guillermo Morales-Luna, Parity balance of the $i$-th dimension edges in Hamiltonian cycles of the hypercube, arXiv:1009.3304 (Theorem 5.2, p. 6))*
- Computing $\alpha_=$ of a bipartite graph reduces in polynomial time to computing the independence number of an auxiliary graph. *(Feliú Sagols, Guillermo Morales-Luna, Parity balance of the $i$-th dimension edges in Hamiltonian cycles of the hypercube, arXiv:1009.3304 (Theorem 5.3, p. 7))*
- Computed values: $\alpha_=(Q_3)=2$, $\alpha_=(Q_4)=4$, $\alpha_=(Q_5)=10$, $\alpha_=(Q_6)=16$, $\alpha_=(Q_7)=40$. The value for $n=8$ was not computed because the auxiliary graph is too large. *(Feliú Sagols, Guillermo Morales-Luna, Parity balance of the $i$-th dimension edges in Hamiltonian cycles of the hypercube, arXiv:1009.3304 (Table 1, p. 7); computational; reproduced: None)*
